headlines.title: Charles Schwab (SCHW) Now Has The Largest U.S. Dividend ETF
headlines.summary: The Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (NYSE:SCHD) has become the largest dividend-focused ETF in the U.S. market. The fund's new status highlights investor interest in Schwab's low-cost, dividend-oriented approach to portfolio income. This positions Charles Schwab's asset management arm as a central player in U.S. dividend ETF product design and distribution. The rise of SCHD to the largest dividend ETF is an important context check alongside the rest of our Charles Schwab work.

headlines.title: How Investors May Respond To Schwab Stock Client Growth And AI Tools
headlines.summary: Charles Schwab recently rolled out AI powered tools, expanded crypto trading to five tokens, upgraded trading platforms, and completed several variable rate bond offerings totaling US$3.0b to support its operations. The mix of generative AI assistants, extended hours options trading, and side by side crypto and traditional investing indicates Schwab’s focus on deeper client engagement and product breadth rather than headline pricing changes.

headlines.title: Charles Schwab (SCHW) Expands AI Tools, Is It Still 22% Below Fair Value?
headlines.summary: Charles Schwab (SCHW) has rolled out a wide set of AI driven tools across Schwab.com, Schwab Mobile and thinkorswim, giving retail clients new ways to analyze portfolios and manage trades directly. Recent price action paints a mixed picture for Charles Schwab. The share price has fallen about 17% over the past 90 days and is down roughly 10% year to date.

headlines.title: Charles Schwab (SCHW) Stock Could Be 31% Undervalued Today
headlines.summary: Charles Schwab has delivered a 70.8% gain over the past 3 years, a run that puts fresh focus on whether the business is earning strong enough returns on its capital to support the current share price. Recent product launches in AI tools, extended trading access and an expanded crypto menu add new storylines, but the core question is still how profitably Schwab is putting client and shareholder capital to work. headlines.summary: A Charles Schwab spokesperson says its brief webpage loading issue is now resolved.

description: The Charles Schwab Corporation, together with its subsidiaries, operates as a savings and loan holding company that provides wealth management, securities brokerage, banking, asset management, custody, and financial advisory services in the United States and internationally. The company operates in two segments, Investor Services and Advisor Services. It offers brokerage accounts with equity and fixed income trading, margin lending, options trading, futures and forex trading, and cash management capabilities, including money market funds, and certificates of deposit; third-party mutual funds through the Mutual Fund Marketplace and Mutual Fund OneSource service, as well as mutual fund trading and clearing services to broker-dealers; exchange-traded funds; advisory solutions for managed portfolios, separately managed accounts, customized personal advice for tailored portfolios, specialized planning, and full-time portfolio management; banking products comprising checking and savings accounts, first lien residential real estate mortgage loans, home equity lines of credit, and pledged asset lines; and trust custody services, personal trust reporting services, and administrative trustee services. It provides digital and software based trading platforms; research tools, and multichannel support, real-time market data, options trading; equity compensation plan sponsors full-service recordkeeping for stock plans, stock options, restricted stock, performance shares, and stock appreciation rights; retirement plan services; mutual fund clearing services; and advisor services, including interactive tools and educational content. The Company operates through branch offices. The Charles Schwab Corporation was founded in 1971 and is headquartered in Westlake, Texas.
